question: The Indira Sagar Multipurpose Project is located in which state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indira Sagar Multipurpose Project is situated in the state of **Madhya Pradesh**, India.
 
• This project is located on the **Narmada River** near the town of Punasa in Khandwa district.
 
• It was inaugurated in **2005** and is one of the largest dam projects in India.
 
• The primary purposes of the Indira Sagar Project include **irrigation, hydroelectric power generation, and water supply**.
 
• The dam has a water storage capacity of approximately **12.22 billion cubic meters**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narmada River**

 
 
• The Narmada River, also known as the Rewa, is one of the major rivers in central India and the fifth-longest river in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It flows westwards over a length of 1,312 km (815 miles) before draining into the Arabian Sea.
 
• The river is often referred to as "the lifeline of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat."
 
 
 
• **Hydroelectric Power Generation**
 
 
• The Indira Sagar Project has a hydroelectric power station with an installed capacity of 1,000 MW.
 
• Hydroelectric power is a renewable source of energy generated by harnessing the potential energy stored in water.
 
• It is a clean source of energy that contributes to reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
 
 
 
• **Irrigation Benefits**
 
 
• The project provides irrigation benefits to an area of approximately 1.23 million hectares in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It ensures the supply of water for agricultural activities, enhancing the productivity and livelihood of farmers in the region.
 
 
 
• **Environmental and Social Impact**
 
 
• Large dam projects like Indira Sagar can have significant environmental and social impacts, including displacement of local communities and changes in the ecosystem.
 
• Efforts are made to mitigate these impacts through resettlement and rehabilitation programs.
